Re-checked at a059b55 (19-orig-state-and-docs.log). D-016 lists what provenance binding actually checks. The resume count is 6 in decisions.md (D-019), agents.md:40, agent-protocol.md:92 and run-agent.sh (MTH_MAX_RESUMES:-6). The other numbers are the 4-worker limit and the in-agent 3-retry rule, which are different things. The protected-path list in agents.md:20-26 matches write-scopes.json protected_for_implementers, using brace and any-depth forms. One remaining documentation inaccuracy (D-021 says evidence 'can no longer be edited in place undetected') belongs to F-DG0-115, not to this finding.

Still bypassable in the round-6 candidate. rules.mjs is byte-identical between d141d303 and a059b55, and my round-5 result (never bound, because that run was orphaned) re-runs identically. The original round-3 vectors are fixed. On 540b3c69, tests 4-6 of the round-3 repro edit a committed sidecar or record to drop a High finding, flip a FAIL verification and flip a FAIL verdict (09-r3). On a059b55, carried tests 3-7 reject those edits: an ordinary-commit rewrite, an uncommitted edit, a verdict flip and the plain evil merge (02-repro-carried-on-a059b55.log). The root-cause design is still defeated by ordering. tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs:606-641 (checkWriteOnce) runs 'git log -m --full-history --diff-filter=A --reverse' (line 609) and keeps as reference the blob of whichever commit that output lists first (lines 610-615). --reverse follows commit ordering, which is influenced by committer dates that the committer chooses freely. It then compares HEAD and the disk only with that blob (lines 633-636) and never looks at M events or at other add events. Carried test 10 (BYPASS N4) passes on a059b55. The runner commits the reviewer's genuine round-2 sidecar (FAIL/OPEN for High F-DG0-101), which keeps the gate closed. A forger then makes side commit S from the freeze commit, with committer date 2001-01-01. S adds the round evidence with a forged PASS/CLOSED_VERIFIED sidecar and a meta.json whose outputs and tool_authored are re-pointed to the forged bytes. The forger merges S with a merge whose tree is the forgery. validateGate(current) then returns []. After approval, validateGate(historical) and validatePipeline return []. 'git diff <round commit> HEAD' shows M on the sidecar. Test 11 (N4b) drops a committed round-1 High finding and flips the round-1 FAIL verdict to PASS the same way. Control test 9: with a current date for S the rewrite is detected, so ordering alone decides. This contradicts D-021 ('every file ever added ... must still hold ... the exact blob that first added it'; 'can no longer be edited in place undetected'), and it is not covered by the disclosed residual, which is fabricating a new run directory as new history; here the genuine blob stays in history. Expected fix: every write-once path has exactly one distinct blob across ALL add/modify events against EVERY parent ('git log -m --full-history --raw'), with no M/T events, and HEAD and the disk equal that blob. Alternatively, reject merges and commits whose committer date precedes a parent's. That rule is satisfiable today: the real history at b6fa2c28 has 224 write-once paths, 0 with more than one blob, 0 merges and 0 back-dated commits (10-history-feasibility.log). Defence in depth: the validator should replay tool_authored from the bound transcript instead of trusting meta.tool_authored. No actual tampering is observed in the real DG0 evidence; this is a control weakness. Severity stays High and mandatory.
